CVE-2026-104199.title: aMQTT: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Improper Input Validation
CVE-2026-104199.description: aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.11.4, add_subscription() in amqtt/broker.py accepts malformed single-level + wildcard placement because it checks substrings instead of validating each slash-delimited level. The _matches() function converts each + into a greedy regular-expression fragment and evaluates it with re.fullmatch(), allowing a filter containing many adjacent + characters to trigger catastrophic backtracking when compared with a topic that partially matches but ultimately fails. Because matching runs synchronously in _run_broadcast(), one subscription followed by a publish can block the broker event loop, stopping message delivery and new connection processing until restart. Anonymous clients can trigger the issue with the default configuration. Any authenticated client permitted to create arbitrary subscriptions and publish messages may still exploit it when authentication is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.4.

CVE-2026-110176.title: File Force Download for Drupal 7 Access Bypass via Unconditional Download Headers
CVE-2026-110176.description:
The File Force Download module for Drupal 7 implements hook_file_download() to add a Content-Disposition header when a file URL carries the download query parameter. In Drupal 7, returning a non-empty header array from that hook is itself a grant of access to the file.

In versions 7.1.0 through 7.1.2, the module only delegated to other modules' hook_file_download() implementations when the file was in the private scheme. For every other scheme it returned its headers without any check. An unauthenticated visitor who appended download=1 to the URL of a file in the temporary:// scheme, or in a stream wrapper supplied by another module, could retrieve the file, overriding the access checks that would otherwise have applied. Files in the public and private schemes are not affected.

CVE-2026-133867.title: @fastify/express vulnerable to middleware bypass via RegExp mount paths under parameterized prefixes
CVE-2026-133867.description: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.7 through 4.0.9, the plugin does not rewrite regular-expression mount paths to account for a parameterized plugin prefix, so when middleware is mounted with a regular expression inside a plugin registered under a parameterized prefix, the Express matcher treats the prefix parameter as literal text and never matches the real request path. As a result, Express silently skips that middleware while Fastify still runs the route handler, so an application that relies on regular-expression mounted middleware for authentication or authorization inside a parameterized-prefix plugin exposes protected routes to unauthenticated clients. No special configuration is required beyond a parameterized prefix and a regular-expression mount. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

CVE-2026-99307.title: ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease
CVE-2026-99307.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: require the dentry lease record to cover struct ceph_mds_reply_lease

parse_reply_info_lease() reads a 32-bit struct_len off the wire and only
checks that many bytes are present, without requiring struct_len to cover
sizeof(struct ceph_mds_reply_lease) (10 bytes). A malicious MDS can
declare a shorter record and still get the pointer published: the
following *p += sizeof(**lease) overshoot is undone by *p = lend, so
nothing downstream rejects the reply. ceph_fill_trace() ->
update_dentry_lease() then reads 10 bytes through that pointer on any
lookup on a mounted CephFS, running past the end of the message front.

Require the record to cover the structure, matching the sibling
parse_reply_info_dir(). A conforming MDS always encodes the full 10
bytes.

BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in __update_dentry_lease.constprop.0 (fs/ceph/inode.c:1459)

CVE-2026-99398.title: xfs: always forget cached ACLs if the attr fork swap succeeds
CVE-2026-99398.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: always forget cached ACLs if the attr fork swap succeeds

LOLLM complains that xrep_xattr_rebuild_tree omits the xfs_forget_acl
call if the attr fork swap succeeds (and hence the acls might have
changed) but reaping the old attr fork fails. Fix it so that we always
purge the cached acls if the swap succeeds, even if subsequent steps do
not. This avoids some cache coherency problems with access controls.
